explain: A UI state machine preserves the difference between receiving partial text and observing authoritative completion. Unknown transitions are rejected rather than guessed.
steps: Declare legal transitions for the task view. || Apply a delta event without marking the task complete.
name: ui-state-machine

explain: A semantic form provides labels and native keyboard controls; CSS changes layout without replacing their behavior. The result area is a restrained completion/status region.
steps: Associate the label and input with matching identifiers. || Use a real submit button and an adaptable layout instead of clickable generic elements.
expect: A labeled question field, submit button, and status area render in a responsive column.
limit: Static browser example; connect its submit event to your validated API before claiming an end-to-end application.
name: semantic-form

explain: Draft text is local UI state while persisted tasks are keyed server state. A new draft must not mutate the saved response record.
steps: Keep separate structures for the draft and saved tasks. || Update the draft and inspect that the saved task remains unchanged.
name: local-server-state

explain: Render model content as text and announce meaningful completion once. Repeated token announcements and arbitrary model HTML can harm accessibility or execute untrusted content.
steps: Use textContent for untrusted model output. || Update a live status region only when the task reaches a meaningful state.
expect: The answer element displays the script-looking text literally; status announces Answer ready.
limit: Browser integration sketch; requires elements with IDs answer and status, and a task object from your validated API.
name: safe-render

explain: Feedback binds to a persisted message identity, not a transient DOM position or the current text. Reloading or rerendering does not change which answer the feedback evaluates.
steps: Resolve the saved message ID. || Create a feedback record referring to that identity and revision.
name: stable-message-feedback

explain: Generate one operation key for an intended mutation and preserve it on retry. A server must enforce uniqueness and payload compatibility; the client key alone provides no exactly-once guarantee.
steps: Allocate the key when the operation is created. || Reuse that operation record for subsequent send attempts.
name: client-operation-key

explain: A source-linked reasoning fixture. JSON parsing checks representation only; reproduce the actual mechanism with the chapter reference.
steps: Inspect the declared input and required invariant. || Trace the chapter mechanism and reproduce the stated case. || Change the stated assumption and defend the result.
expect: Reasoning input only; no program result is claimed. Reproduce the scenario using the chapter’s runnable reference.
limit: A JSON case is parsed for representation integrity only, not executed as a proof of its semantic claim.
